idiom_name: private fields assigned once + validating constructor/factory + query-only interface + copy-with methods
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: hold every member privately, assign it exactly once in a constructor or factory that validates the invariants and copies any mutable argument, and expose no method that changes state; a logical update is a copy-with method that constructs a new instance sharing the untouched parts. Freeze the type so no subtype can add mutable state, make queries return immutable views or copies rather than interior references, and keep the deep state immutable or copied so the guarantee is not shallow. Where construction is multi-step, gather the parts in a mutable builder and freeze once at the end; where the value is large and updated often, use a persistent representation with structural sharing instead of deep copies.
code_sketch:
value  = Money.of(1999, "EUR")          # validate and copy on the way in
price  = value.plus(Money.of(555, "EUR"))    # returns a new value; value is unchanged
# class Money: private members, no setters, equality and hash from the content,
# queries never hand out mutable interior state
pitfalls: Shipping the classic structure but returning interior mutable state (lists, arrays, dates) from queries: the guarantee is only as deep as the shallowest accessor.
Forgetting to freeze the type: a subclass that adds mutable state makes every instance mutable for code holding the base type.
Copying the whole graph on every update instead of sharing the unchanged parts, which replaces the mutation cost with a worse copy cost.
Publishing the instance before construction completes (this escape, non-final fields, lazy state), so other threads observe a half-built value.

Assuming final fields make deep immutability: final prevents reassignment of the reference but says nothing about the mutability of the object it points to. A final List field still accepts add(); a final Date still has setters.

Using Collections.unmodifiableList() as a getter return when the underlying source list is owned by another thread or object: the view reflects source mutations. Use List.copyOf() for a true snapshot.
Validating a mutable argument before copying it (TOCTOU race): if a caller mutates the argument between validation and the copy, the invariant is silently broken. Copy first, then validate.

Relying on language keywords or frozen flags alone without checking contained types: in Python, frozen=True on a dataclass with a list field still allows list.append(); in Java, a final field of type Date is still mutable via date.setTime().

Shallow copying nested mutable objects: List.copyOf() copies the container but not the elements. If contained elements are mutable, external code holding an element reference can mutate the logical state of the supposedly immutable parent.

In Java records with mutable component types, the compact constructor does not defensively copy by default: a record Point(List<Integer> coords) stores the List reference directly, so callers holding that List can mutate the record's state after construction.

In Java, Serialization.readObject can be replaced by the record canonical constructor path — this is more secure but means all validation must happen in the canonical constructor; any validation placed only in a traditional readObject is bypassed on deserialisation.

Java framework reflection mutating final fields: Hibernate, Jackson, and Spring have historically used setAccessible(true) to modify final fields after construction, silently breaking immutability guarantees. Java 16+ restricts this for records, but non-record classes remain vulnerable.

In C# record struct, forgetting the readonly modifier leaves properties mutable: var r = new PointRecordStruct(); r.X = 5; // compiles and mutates in place — use readonly record struct to make all property setters init-only.

In C#, with-expressions perform shallow copies only — a record with a mutable object field (e.g., List<string>) shares the list reference between original and copy; mutating the list through either reference is a data race in concurrent code.

Kotlin data class with a MutableList constructor parameter declared as val still allows list operations: data class Box(val items: MutableList<String>); val box = Box(mutableListOf()); box.items.add("x") — use List instead of MutableList and copy on construction.

Swift struct with let properties but a property of class type still allows mutation of the class instance: the let binding is to the class reference, not to the class's internal state — use value types (Array, Dictionary) for truly immutable collection fields.

Swift copy-on-write semantics mean that for large structs, copying is deferred until mutation — a withAnimation or transform that copies a large struct may introduce unexpected aliasing in concurrent code until the copy actually occurs.

Go functional options applied in order may have conflicting effects if later options assume earlier ones have already run — a Logger option applied before a Level option may log at the wrong level during construction; document the application order contract explicitly.

Immutable objects containing non-hashable elements (e.g., a Python list inside a frozen dataclass) silently make the parent unhashable, breaking use as dict keys or set members. Always use tuple/frozenset for collection fields in hashable immutables.

TOCTOU on construction validation: validating a mutable argument and then storing it without copying allows a concurrent caller to mutate the argument between validation and the store. Always copy first, validate on the copy.

Equality and hash computation over mutable collection fields: if a field is a list at construction time but is replaced with a frozenset later, equal instances computed before the replacement have different hashes — use immutable field types from the start.

Immutable object interning with weak references: if an intern pool uses WeakValueDictionary, garbage collection can evict instances that are still logically in use, causing duplicate equal instances to appear. Use strong references for canonical instance pools.

Deep freezing a nested structure at runtime (e.g., Python dataclasses.replace with deepcopy) is O(n) in total size per update — for large nested graphs, this can dominate update costs; persistent data structures with structural sharing keep update cost near O(log n).

Wrong move: Treat Java records, C# records, or frozen wrappers as deep immutability -> nested lists and maps remain aliased and can mutate equality or hash state through another reference -> instead copy mutable inputs before validation and store immutable component types or persistent collections such as PMap or immutables.Map.
sources: Grand, M., Patterns in Java: A Catalog of Reusable Design Patterns Illustrated with UML, Vol. 1 (Wiley, 1998) - the Immutable pattern: an object whose state information cannot change after it is constructed, used to avoid access coordination between threads.
Henney, K., Immutable Value (BCS OOPS Patterns Day 1998; workshopped at PLoP 98) - https://c2.com/ppr/wiki/JavaIdioms/ImmutableValue.html
Bloch, J., Effective Java, 3rd ed. (Addison-Wesley, 2018), Item 17 Minimize mutability and Item 50 Make defensive copies when needed.
https://github.com/iluwatar/java-design-patterns/blob/master/immutable/README.md
https://www.artima.com/interfacedesign/Immutable.html
Oracle Java Tutorial, A Strategy for Defining Immutable Objects - https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/essential/concurrency/imstrat.html
Error Prone @Immutable checker - http://errorprone.info/bugpattern/Immutable.html

Birka, A. and Ernst, M.D., A Practical Type System and Language for Reference Immutability, OOPSLA 2004 - introduces Javari, a reference-immutability type system for Java where readonly references guarantee the transitively reachable state cannot be modified through that reference; statically prevents entire classes of mutation bugs.

Kohol, D. et al., Constrictor: Immutability as a Design Concept, ECOOP 2024 (LIPIcs) - presents view-immutability: an object is immutable from the perspective of its exposed view methods even if internal state mutates; implemented as an SMT-based linter/verifier; relevant for Python where frozen only prevents rebinding but allows internal mutation.

Kjolstad, F. et al., Transformation for Class Immutability, Illinois/OOPSLA 2007 - Immutator: an Eclipse-based tool and algorithm for automatically converting mutable Java classes to immutable ones via inter-procedural mutator analysis and escape analysis; studies show manual conversion introduces 6.37 bugs/class on average vs. zero for the tool.

Riehle, D., Value Object, PLoP 2006 (riehle.org/computer-science/research/2006/plop-2006-value-object.pdf) - formalises Value Object as a pattern: immutable objects used as value types, with participants (Client, Value), applicability trade-offs, and implementation notes on identity/equality, interning, and enum-based value types.

Ramalho, L., Fluent Python, 2nd ed. (O'Reilly, 2022) - covers Pythonic implementation of immutable objects including dataclass(frozen=True), NamedTuple semantics, protocol-based duck typing, and __slots__; essential reference for idiomatic Python immutable object patterns.

attrs Authors, attrs Documentation: Immutability - https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/api.html - official attrs documentation on the frozen parameter, FrozenInstanceError, frozen slotted classes performance cost, and the attrs.setters.frozen hook for per-attribute immutability.
attrs Authors, attrs Documentation: Hashing - https://attrs.org/en/stable/api.html - covers hash method generation, hashing and mutability, and hash code caching for frozen attrs classes.

Pydantic Authors, Pydantic Documentation: Faux Immutability - https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/models/ - documents ConfigDict(frozen=True) and the shallow nature of Pydantic's immutability: dict fields can still be mutated even when the model is frozen.

Real Python, Data Classes in Python (Guide) - https://realpython.com/python-data-classes/ - comprehensive Real Python tutorial covering frozen=True, shallow immutability gotchas, nested mutable fields, and field(default_factory=...) patterns.

TheCodeForge, Dataclasses - Mutable Default Traps That Break Prod - https://thecodeforge.io/python/dataclasses-python/ - production-focused dataclass pitfalls: mutable defaults, frozen+computed fields, __post_init__ assignment in frozen dataclasses, and __hash__ generation rules.

EngineersOfAI, Immutability Strategies - Tuples, Frozen Dataclasses, and Value Objects - https://engineersofai.com/docs/python/python-intermediate/functional-programming/immutability-strategies - covers frozen=True shallow immutability, tuple vs list for collection fields, dataclasses.replace() functional update pattern, and deep immutability composition.

EngineersOfAI, Dataclasses - Code Generation, Immutability, and Production Patterns - https://engineersofai.com/docs/python/python-intermediate/object-oriented-programming/dataclasses - covers frozen=True, __post_init__, field(default_factory=...), kw_only=True, inheritance field ordering rules, and NamedTuple vs frozen dataclass tradeoffs.

Cursa, Immutability, Freezing, and Controlled Mutation - https://cursa.app/en/page/immutability-freezing-and-controlled-mutation - covers shallow vs deep immutability, MappingProxyType for dict views, pydantic frozen, object.__setattr__ for internal caching in frozen dataclasses, and controlled mutation patterns.

Johal, A., Immutable Data Structures in Python with Frozen Dataclasses 2026 - https://johal.in/immutable-data-structures-in-python-with-frozen-dataclasses-2026 - production case study: frozen dataclasses for transaction DTOs in a 10K tx/sec system, recursive freezing for nested structures, and performance benchmarking with pypersistent.

Application Architect, Python Frozen Dataclasses: Immutable Data Objects - https://www.application-architect.com/posts/python-frozen-dataclasses-immutable-data-objects/ - covers frozen=True auto-generated __hash__, shallow immutability, nested frozen dataclass composition, and minimal performance overhead measurements.

Pyrsistent Authors, Pyrsistent Documentation - https://pyrsistent.readthedocs.io/ - provides PVector, PMap, PSet, PRecord, and PClass persistent/functional data structures with structural sharing; evolvers provide controlled mutable access before freezing.

PyPersistent Authors, PyPersistent Documentation - https://pypi.org/project/pypersistent/ - high-performance persistent data structures (C++ HAMT-based PersistentDict, PersistentList, PersistentSet) with structural sharing, free-threaded CPython 3.13+ support, and O(log n) update operations.

MagicStack, immutables Library - https://github.com/MagicStack/immutables/ - HAMT-based immutable mapping used internally by CPython contextvars (PEP 550/567); provides Map and Set with O(log N) operations and structural sharing.

Python core team, PEP 818 - Add frozendict built-in type - https://peps.python.org/pep-0814/ - proposes adding frozendict to the builtins module; hashable when all keys and values are hashable; preserves insertion order; avoids the pitfalls of MappingProxyType (not hashable, can be reached via gc.get_referents).
